audits.text:
## 74d1cf8c8502

**Actionable shortcut: generated support never distinguishes 4-connectivity from 8-connectivity.** The audited source SHA-256 is `6e970f1fe6915843f8e87472589b0598652018536327b9edd1a695d22de6ca20`; rule hash `a17667e8f90e`.

The intended rule outlines each 4-connected magenta object independently. A plausible rival first merges diagonally touching magenta cells into 8-connected objects, then outlines each merged bounding box. That rival fits all 3 canonical pairs and all 600 sampled generated inputs checked (200 indices in each of easy, medium, and hard at seed `90210`). The current sampler enforces a one-cell moat between object bounding boxes, so the distinction never appears; the current declared semantic gate nevertheless passes because this rival is undeclared.

The retained 10×12 witness has two 4-connected components but one 8-connected component. Public Racket output and the independent intended mirror agree, while the rival differs in 8 cells; the first zero-based difference is `(2,4)`, intended `0`, rival `2`. Current `self_check` rejects only the missing moat, so the witness is lawful for the selected Racket expression but outside the sampler/validator domain.

Evidence and reproduction: `checks/audit/74d1cf8c8502/probe-report.json`, `checks/audit/74d1cf8c8502/input.json`, `checks/audit/74d1cf8c8502/rival.json`, `checks/audit/74d1cf8c8502/racket.json`, and probe source `checks/audit/74d1cf8c8502/probe.py`. The existing declared contract pass is retained at `checks/audit/74d1cf8c8502-semantic/result.json`. Recommended repair: add diagonal-touching but 4-disconnected examples, declare the 8-connected merger rival, and relax only the moat restriction needed to materialize those witnesses.
